assessment.nobel_worthiness: The credit-cycles model of Kiyotaki and Moore shows how collateral constraints and asset prices amplify and propagate shocks. It became a foundation for macro-finance, financial-friction DSGE models and policy analysis after the 2008 crisis. The idea is general, tractable and central to how macroeconomists think about credit.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (JPE 1997) are the clearest originators of the collateral-constraint dynamic mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the adjacent financial-accelerator tradition, whose most prominent contribution was already recognised in 2022 through related work on financial crises. Limiting the award to the first two keeps attribution clean.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of citation, extension and empirical use. The 2008 crisis and later work confirmed its relevance, so the timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Gertler and Gilchrist as the financial-accelerator strand.
Overlap with the 2022 financial-intermediation recognition could be read as lowering marginal novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting transformed international trade. They created a new channel for gains from trade and a micro-founded framework that links theory to firm-level data. The work has had broad influence on empirical trade and on policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (Econometrica 2003) is the central originator of the heterogeneous-firm model, and Helpman has a long record of foundational trade theory and of extending the firm-level framework. Redding is a major contributor to quantitative and spatial extensions, but his role is more derivative of the core insight.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of use. The framework is standard in graduate teaching and in applied work.
uncertainties: Bernard, Eaton, Kortum and Jensen made closely related empirical and theoretical contributions that are not credited on this ballot entry, so priority may be contested.
Quantitative trade models, which are on the longlist separately, may overlap with this strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis. They cover staggered pricing and contracts, policy rules and the micro-founded framework used by central banks. The practical and intellectual reach of this work is very large.
assessment.attribution: The ballot entry credits eight people, so the award must be restricted to three. Calvo (time-dependent pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (the synthesis and optimal-policy theory) are the most defensible core. Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets made important and often decisive contributions to estimation and extension, and leaving them out is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. The framework has been the dominant paradigm for decades and has been tested through several policy regimes, including the post-2008 and post-pandemic inflation episodes.
uncertainties: The attribution problem is severe: any three-person selection omits several highly deserving contributors, and previous prizes already cover related ground (rational expectations, Phillips curve, time inconsistency).
Post-2021 inflation experience prompted debate about how well the framework fits, though that does not reduce the historical contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the measurement of trade shocks reshaped understanding of wage inequality and polarization. The China-shock work showed durable local labor-market effects, and the task framework changed how automation is analysed. The topic is central to current policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the clearest common thread across the task approach and the trade-shock studies. Hanson was central to the trade-shock empirical program with Autor and Dorn. Katz and Dorn also made major contributions, and the task-framework theory owes much to Acemoglu and Restrepo, who are not credited on this entry.
assessment.maturity: Highly influential, with roughly fifteen to twenty-five years of development. Some of the results on persistent effects and on the task framework are still being debated and refined.
uncertainties: Theoretical credit for the task framework is partly outside the credited names.
Empirical robustness of some trade-shock estimates is still under discussion.
A close overlap with the skill-biased technical change literature, to which Katz and Goldin contributed, complicates attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand with differentiated products and for estimating dynamic industry models made structural empirical industrial organization practical. They are the basis for merger analysis, antitrust and many applied studies. Impact is large and operates through widely used tools.
assessment.attribution: The BLP demand framework (Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes) is clearly attributable to these three. Pakes also has foundational dynamic-games work with Ericson and with others. The ballot lists seven names, so Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin would be omitted despite meaningful contributions.
assessment.maturity: Mature. BLP has been used for three decades and has been extended in many directions.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this primarily as methodology or as substantive economic discovery.
Selection among the seven credited names is contestable.
Identification debates about instruments and about functional form remain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation research quantified how distortions in the allocation of inputs across firms can explain a large share of cross-country income differences. It produced a widely used measurement framework in growth and development. The core insight is simple and generalizes to many settings.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (QJE 2009) are the source of the canonical measurement exercise. Restuccia and Rogerson developed a closely related theoretical formulation, and Restuccia is credited here. Because Rogerson is not credited, the shared priority is incomplete, and I keep the proposal to the measurement pair.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of influence. The magnitude of the effects is still debated because of measurement error and the interpretation of dispersion in marginal products.
uncertainties: Measurement concerns about whether dispersion in revenue productivity reflects true distortions.
Priority relative to Restuccia and Rogerson and to the earlier theory literature.
I have a general interest in the macro-development field, so the committee should weigh my judgment accordingly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data brought new measurement of intergenerational mobility and of place effects on children's outcomes. The work has had substantial influence on public debate and on research methodology. Its scientific content is partly empirical measurement rather than a new theoretical principle.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the leading figure across the mobility atlas and related studies, and Hendren is central to the place-effects work. Friedman and Katz contributed to the broader program. The ballot mixes different papers and teams, so a narrow selection is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young. The main results are from roughly the last decade, and long-run replication, causal interpretation of place effects and policy lessons are still maturing.
uncertainties: Timing: the work may be better recognised after more years of validation.
Credit is spread across a large collaborative group.
Chetty's work spans other topics that may be considered separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression is a widely used method for analysing distributional effects. It is applied across labor, finance and other empirical fields. As a methodological contribution it matches the type of econometric recognition given previously, though it is less transformative than the top-ranked substantive ideas.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (Econometrica 1978) introduced the estimator, and Koenker developed the broader theory and software. Chernozhukov is credited for later inferential work but has other contributions that might be recognised separately, so I keep the proposal to the originators.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with more than four decades of use and broad validation.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards this as sufficiently broad in intellectual impact compared with substantive discoveries.
Chernozhukov appears in several longlist entries, which complicates how credit should be allocated.
